This isn’t a shooter, it’s a social experiment with capes and spandex. You jump in expecting to feel like a superhero, and within two minutes you’re stuck in a match where Rocket Raccoon humiliates you from five kilometers away while Hulk dances on your corpse. Gameplay is this weird mix of trying to be Overwatch and trying to sell you skins that would make Tony Stark blush. Balance? Optional. Strategy? Also optional. What really matters here is throwing colorful beams everywhere and praying your connection doesn't die in the middle of a combo attack nobody asked for but everyone suffers through. A brilliant chaos where every match reminds you that, at the end of the day, we’re all just background characters in Deadpool’s show.

QUALIFICATION
8/10 TIGHT STOCKINGS

Marvel Rivals shines in its creative direction, cosmetics, and varied game modes that stretch well beyond standard objective play into fun arcade mashups and seasonal events. However, the core gameplay and player base don't always hit the mark.

While those extra modes give you a decent break from the norm, the game's biggest issue lies in the competitive matchmaking, which frequently feels completely disconnected from individual performance. Despite putting up immense damage or healing numbers, matches often feel out of your hands, making ranked progression feel overly randomized and RNG-based. The egos within the player base only compound these issues, as people routinely refuse to switch off their mains or adjust team comps for the objective, leaving match outcomes pretty much up to chance. Character progression and unlocks are also extremely time consuming and feel unrewarding.

When team comps somehow click, the ultimates stack perfectly, and you're rolling through lobbies, it's easy to forget all of those flaws. Ranked is an absolute blast when you're the one handing out the Ls, but once the win streak ends, you're quickly reminded of the game's underlying issues.

6.5/10 - creative, unbalanced, inaccurate or randomized competitive results

I came to Marvel Rivals as a huge Marvel fan, but this game is honestly disappointing.

The balance is terrible. The support role isn’t enjoyable at all, and matches feel heavily skewed depending on team composition. Some roles clearly have way more impact than others.

The worst part is the matchmaking. It’s completely unfair and unbalanced. Games are often one-sided stomps with huge skill gaps between players. It doesn’t feel competitive — it feels frustrating.

This game has potential, but right now it’s badly balanced and the matchmaking ruins the experience. I can’t recommend it.

It's got a lot of different elements that could lead to a lot of different games, giving each game it's own "touches" — but ultimately you'll end up doing the same things since damage is generally too high and supports need to heal equally as much. Team-ups don't generally emphasize "Teamplay" and are typically circumstantial. In the circumstances you *do* choose to use a team-up, it's typically because it gives one player a game defining ability — which is cool in theory, but with the only requirement being having someone pick the character makes it very insipid. 
While I voted negatively, this is mostly due to playing for awhile and not seeing things change. As a new player, I think you could get plenty of enjoyment from the characters, style, and unique character design philosophies. As someone who's spent 500 hours on it though — it's monotony keeps surfacing every time I come back to the game.
